findings.text: Each listed header defines a distinct inclusion guard marker so repeated inclusion has no further effect. The guards carry no behavioral semantics beyond idempotence.

Tracer capability advertisement uses numeric value 1 for operations support and shifted stack tracer handling, with presence markers for graph frame pointer testing, register tracing, compat syscall ignoring, and symbolic syscall name matching.
Patch size for the compiler hook equals the architectural instruction width, the tracer linkage area has index 0 and total count 1, and the hook address derives from the compiler inserted symbol.

Futex retry exhaustion bound is 128 iterations, interrupt exit is declared to run with interrupts disabled via value 1, and supported shadow stack status combines enable plus write plus push permissions.
Dynamic tracer needs no architecture private per site storage on this port, expressed as an empty record with no members.

Tracer register snapshot holds nine general slots plus one configuration dependent slot for direct trampoline address or unused storage, followed by separate holders for frame pointer and return link and stack pointer and program counter.
Nonmaskable context holder pairs a 64 bit saved hypervisor control value with an unsigned event counter.

Accessors view an opaque tracer handle as the architecture snapshot. Instruction, stack, frame, and return link getters return the matching stored fields, argument fetch serves the first eight general slots and yields zero above that, return value access uses the first general slot, setters update program counter or first slot, and generic trap register conversion yields nothing.

Two narrowing conversions export only a subset into wider views. Partial conversion copies the nine general slots with stack and program values, places frame and link into the conventional callee saved positions, and forces privileged kernel mode. Performance conversion fills program plus frame plus stack plus privileged mode in the destination.
Byte copying in this scope is an alias forwarding destination plus source plus length to the architecture optimized implementation.

Function override replaces the saved program address with the saved return link so execution resumes at the caller. Direct call support stores a caller supplied trampoline address into the configuration dependent slot for later return redirection. Symbol lookup, return address query, and no operation plus graph hooks are direct aliases to architecture or generic helpers.

Compat system calls are excluded from tracing consideration, with compat status decided by task state. Symbolic matching compensates for a fixed eight character architecture prefix on syscall symbols before comparing against the requested name.

Two user memory entry points validate that a four byte user object is addressable, normalize the pointer by clearing a high tag bit, then delegate internally. The multiplexed operation supports set and add and or and and-not and xor, negating the operand for and-not and reporting not supported for other codes. The compare exchange variant forwards expected and replacement values and reports the observed value.

Atomic selection chooses between single instruction and exclusive monitor implementations according to a hardware capability probe when available, otherwise it always uses the exclusive monitor path. Thin wrappers forward each named operation and compare exchange through this selector.

Exclusive monitor helpers run a bounded retry loop around load exclusive plus transform plus store exclusive inside a privileged user access window, followed by an ordering barrier. User faults divert to a common exit through exception entries, success publishes the observed old value, contention consumes the remaining budget, and exhaustion reports retryable failure.

Single instruction helpers execute one acquiring atomic memory update inside a temporary user table window and report the fetched old value. Narrow compare exchange is emulated by aligning down to 64 bits, preserving the untouched half, and attempting a wide compare exchange, translating wide mismatch into retryable failure while still returning the observed half. Exclusive or is a bounded retry loop over that narrow primitive, logical and is built by inverting into and-not, and four named operations cover add, bit set, bit clear, and swap.

Privileged user access windows open by enabling tag check override then either enabling the user table or disabling hardware address protection, and close in reverse by disabling tag override then either disabling the user table or enabling hardware protection. When the corresponding features are absent the tag and table helpers become no operation predicates reporting no action.

User table switching masks interrupts across the register sequence and issues a synchronization barrier before restoring interrupts. Disable installs a reserved table with cleared identifier, while enable restores the saved user table and merges its identifier into the active kernel table after sampling under the same mask.

Address validity first removes tagging for kernel threads or tagged address tasks before delegating to the generic range check. Separately, user pointers are sanitized by clearing a single high order bit.

Guarded stack primitives provide a barrier ordering prior guarded operations, a guarded store of a value to an address, and two control moves that push a value into and pull a value from dedicated guarded stack state.

Enable status tests a mode flag in thread storage, and locked updates are rejected as busy when the masked new value differs from the masked current value under the thread lock mask. Builds without support report disabled, accept lock checks trivially, do nothing for mode set and free and state preserve and user push and put, fail user fetch, fail thread stack allocation as unsupported, and return zero for user pop.

User guarded word transfer validates the destination range, opens a temporary user table window around a guarded store with fault capture, then closes the window and propagates failures. Push reserves one word by decrementing the user guarded pointer before storing and only commits the new pointer on success. Fetch orders prior guarded operations before copying one word out, and pop reads at the current pointer before advancing it on success.

A futex user operation moves from validation and pointer normalization into repeated atomic attempts. Each attempt ends in success with old value publication, address fault with abort, contention with budgeted retry, or budget exhaustion with retryable failure for the caller to handle.

Concurrent updates to the same futex word can force repeated exclusive failures until the bounded budget is exhausted, and any user fault inside atomic or guarded windows diverts to an error exit without updating the published old value or guarded pointer. Restoring user tables races identifier rollover unless interrupts stay masked across sampling and programming.

External callers can rely on the multiplexed futex operation and inatomic compare exchange, the tracer register getters and setters with override and partial conversions, the bad interrupt acknowledgment alias, and the guarded stack push, pop, fetch, store, mode, and lock helpers.
